evals.name: choose-modularity-for-growing-monolith
evals.prompt: Our 80k-line app has one team and one deployment, but checkout changes regularly break reporting. Inspect the repository before proposing how to reorganize it. Should we split into services? Give a practical design and migration plan.
evals.expected_output: The response asks for or inspects repository evidence, chooses a modular monolith unless operational constraints justify services, proposes vertical slices with owned data and dependency direction, and includes boundary checks and stop signals.
assertions: It does not recommend microservices solely because the codebase is large
It names a concrete pressure and an incremental migration path
It includes at least one boundary or fitness check and an explicit stop signal

evals.name: validate-service-extraction
evals.prompt: We want to extract billing from a monolith. Billing and orders currently share six tables and callers reach into billing internals. Design the module boundary and safest extraction sequence.
evals.expected_output: The response identifies shared data and internal coupling as blockers, defines ownership and a narrow contract, recommends branch by abstraction or a strangler path with rollout and rollback, and avoids simultaneous writes without reconciliation.
assertions: It treats shared tables as an ownership problem rather than simply adding an API
It specifies contract, rollout, rollback, and deletion criteria
It proposes boundary validation for forbidden internals or data access

evals.name: stop-premature-splitting
evals.prompt: A small two-person product team asks for 14 microservices so each feature has its own module. The product has one release cadence and no independent scaling needs. Respond with a recommendation and what to do instead.
evals.expected_output: The response recommends a single module or modular monolith with explicit vertical seams, explains the operational cost of services, and gives criteria for revisiting the decision.
assertions: It rejects service-per-feature as premature without operational or ownership evidence
It proposes a proportionate lower rung and vertical slices
It states concrete conditions that would justify later extraction
